units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
BARBARA [impulsively going to her and kissing her] No, no: God help you, dear, you must: you are saving the Army.
Go; and may you have a great meeting!
But arn't you coming?
units.name: JENNY

units.text: No.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She begins taking off the silver brooch from her collar.
Barbara: what are you doing?
units.name: MRS BAINES

units.text: Why are you taking your badge off? You can't be going to leave us, Major.
units.name: JENNY

units.text: BARBARA [quietly] Father: come here.
UNDERSHAFT [coming to her] My dear! [Seeing that she is going to pin the badge on his collar, he retreats to the penthouse in some alarm].
BARBARA [following him] Don't be frightened. [She pins the badge on and steps back towards the table, showing him to the others] There!
It's not much for 5000 pounds is it?
Barbara: if you won't come and pray with us, promise me you will pray for us.
units.name: MRS BAINES

units.text: I can't pray now. Perhaps I shall never pray again.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Barbara!
units.name: MRS BAINES

units.text: Major!
units.name: JENNY

units.text: BARBARA [almost delirious] I can't bear any more.
Quick march!
CUSINS [calling to the procession in the street outside] Off we go.
Play up, there!
Immenso giubilo. [He gives the time with his drum; and the band strikes up the march, which rapidly becomes more distant as the procession moves briskly away].
I must go, dear. You're overworked: you will be all right tomorrow. We'll never lose you. Now Jenny: step out with the old flag. Blood and Fire!
units.name: MRS BAINES

units.text: She marches out through the gate with her flag.
Glory Hallelujah!
units.name: JENNY

units.text: flourishing her tambourine and marching.
UNDERSHAFT [to Cusins, as he marches out past him easing the slide of his trombone] "My ducats and my daughter"!
CUSINS [following him out] Money and gunpowder!
Drunkenness and Murder! My God: why hast thou forsaken me?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She sinks on the form with her face buried in her hands.
The march passes away into silence.
Bill Walker steals across to her.
BILL [taunting] Wot prawce Selvytion nah?
Don't you hit her when she's down.
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: She it me wen aw wiz dahn. Waw shouldn't I git a bit o me own back?
units.name: BILL

units.text: BARBARA [raising her head] I didn't take your money, Bill. [She crosses the yard to the gate and turns her back on the two men to hide her face from them].
BILL [sneering after her] Naow, it warn't enough for you. [Turning to the drum, he misses the money].
Ellow!
If you ain't took it summun else az.
Were's it gorn?
Blame me if Jenny Ill didn't take it arter all!
RUMMY [screaming at him from the loft] You lie, you dirty blackguard!
Snobby Price pinched it off the drum wen e took ap iz cap.
I was ap ere all the time an see im do it.
Wot! Stowl maw money! Waw didn't you call thief on him, you silly old mucker you?
units.name: BILL

units.text: To serve you aht for ittin me acrost the face. It's cost y'pahnd, that az.
units.name: RUMMY

units.text: Raising a paean of squalid triumph.
I done you. I'm even with you. I've ad it aht o y--.
units.name: RUMMY

units.text: Bill snatches up Shirley's mug and hurls it at her.
She slams the loft door and vanishes.
The mug smashes against the door and falls in fragments.
BILL [beginning to chuckle] Tell us, ole man, wot o'clock this morrun was it wen im as they call Snobby Prawce was sived?
BARBARA [turning to him more composedly, and with unspoiled sweetness] About half past twelve, Bill.
And he pinched your pound at a quarter to two.
I know.
Well, you can't afford to lose it.
I'll send it to you.
BILL [his voice and accent suddenly improving] Not if I was to starve for it.
I ain't to be bought.
Ain't you? You'd sell yourself to the devil for a pint o beer; ony there ain't no devil to make the offer.
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: BILL [unshamed] So I would, mate, and often av, cheerful.
But she cawn't buy me. [Approaching Barbara] You wanted my soul, did you?
Well, you ain't got it.
I nearly got it, Bill. But we've sold it back to you for ten thousand pounds.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: And dear at the money!
units.name: SHIRLEY

units.text: No, Peter: it was worth more than money.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [salvationproof] It's no good: you cawn't get rahnd me nah.
I don't blieve in it; and I've seen today that I was right. [Going] So long, old soupkitchener!
Ta, ta, Major Earl's Grendorter! [Turning at the gate] Wot prawce Selvytion nah?
Snobby Prawce!
Ha! ha!
BARBARA [offering her hand] Goodbye, Bill.
BILL [taken aback, half plucks his cap off then shoves it on again defiantly] Git aht. [Barbara drops her hand, discouraged.
He has a twinge of remorse].
But thet's aw rawt, you knaow.
Nathink pasnl.
Naow mellice.
So long, Judy. [He goes].
